topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.10(3), where are the fees for examinations and licenses granted under ch. 452 specified, and how is the renewal fee determined?
choice_a: Examination and license fees are specified under s. 440.05, and the renewal fee is determined by the department under s. 440.03(9)(a)
choice_b: Fees are set annually by the Real Estate Examining Board without any statutory cross-reference
choice_c: All fees, including renewal fees, are fixed permanently within the text of ch. 452 itself
choice_d: The renewal fee is set by the Board of Regents of the University of Wisconsin System
explanation: Section 452.10(3) states: 'The fees for examinations and licenses granted under this chapter are specified under s. 440.05, and the renewal fee for such licenses is determined by the department under s. 440.03 (9) (a).'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.10(6), what discretion does the board have regarding applications for renewal of a license?
choice_a: The board must hold a public hearing before dispensing with any application requirement for a renewal
choice_b: The board may dispense with matters contained in s. 452.09(1) that it deems unnecessary in view of the applicant's prior applications
choice_c: The board must always require the full new-application content under s. 452.09(1) at every renewal, with no exceptions
choice_d: The board may waive continuing education requirements at its own discretion for any renewal applicant
explanation: Section 452.10(6) provides: 'In the case of applications for renewals of licenses the board may dispense with such matters contained in s. 452.09 (1) as it deems unnecessary in view of prior applications.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.11(1), how may a nonresident become a licensed Wisconsin broker or salesperson?
choice_a: Automatically, upon proof of current licensure as a broker or salesperson in the applicant's home state
choice_b: Only if the nonresident secures a Wisconsin-resident broker to co-sign the application
choice_c: By conforming to all the provisions of ch. 452 that apply to any other applicant
choice_d: Only through a reciprocal agreement; nonresidents may never apply through the standard application process
explanation: Section 452.11(1) states: 'A nonresident may become a broker or salesperson by conforming to all the provisions of this chapter.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(2)(c), an initial application for a broker's license to be issued to a business entity must be made on forms prescribed by the board listing what, and accompanied by what fee?
choice_a: Only the name of the entity's registered agent, accompanied by a flat $10 filing fee
choice_b: Only the name of a single managing broker, with no fee required at the time of initial application
choice_c: The entity's federal tax identification number, accompanied by the transfer fee under s. 440.05(7)
choice_d: The names and addresses of all business representatives and the license numbers of all business representatives who are licensed brokers, accompanied by the initial credential fee determined by the department under s. 440.03(9)(a)
explanation: Section 452.12(2)(c) provides that the application 'shall be made on forms prescribed by the board, listing the names and addresses of all business representatives and the license numbers of all business representatives that are licensed brokers, and shall be accompanied by the initial credential fee determined by the department under s. 440.03 (9) (a).'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(5)(a), which licenses are subject to the renewal-application and fee deadline tied to the renewal date specified under s. 440.08(2)(a)?
choice_a: Renewal applications for all licenses issued under ch. 452, whether issued to individuals or to firms
choice_b: Only individual broker and salesperson licenses; firm licenses have no fixed renewal deadline
choice_c: Only firm licenses; individual licenses renew automatically without a deadline
choice_d: Only licenses that have already been renewed at least once before
explanation: Section 452.12(5)(a) states: 'Renewal applications for all licenses shall be submitted with the applicable renewal fee determined by the department under s. 440.03 (9) (a) on or before the applicable renewal date specified under s. 440.08 (2) (a).'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(5)(bm)1, if a firm's license renewal application is not timely filed or the renewal is not granted, what may the firm not do?
choice_a: Maintain its interest-bearing common trust account, though all other activities remain permitted
choice_b: Engage in any of the activities covered by the license until the license is renewed or a new license is issued
choice_c: Continue operating for up to 90 days under an automatic statutory grace period
choice_d: Hire any new salespersons, though it may otherwise continue normal brokerage operations
explanation: Section 452.12(5)(bm)1 provides that if a firm's renewal application is not filed on or before the renewal date or the renewal is not granted, 'the firm may not engage in any of the activities covered by the license until the license is renewed or a new license is issued.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(5)(bm)2, when a firm's license renewal is not granted, what is the effect on licensees associated with that firm?
choice_a: Licensees associated with the firm automatically become independent practitioners for the duration of the lapse
choice_b: Each associated licensee's own individual license is automatically suspended along with the firm's license
choice_c: Those licensees may not engage in any of the activities covered by the firm's license on behalf of the firm until the firm's license is renewed or a new license is issued
choice_d: Only the firm's supervising broker is restricted; other associated licensees may continue working on the firm's behalf
explanation: Section 452.12(5)(bm)2 provides that 'any licensees associated with the firm may not engage in any of the activities covered by the firm's license on behalf of the firm until the firm's license is renewed or a new license is issued.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.12(5)(d), in addition to submitting proof of continuing education, what must each individual broker or salesperson do at the time of renewal?
choice_a: Submit a new criminal background check obtained from a private background-check vendor
choice_b: Obtain notarization of the renewal application by a Wisconsin notary public
choice_c: Pass a supplemental renewal examination administered by the board
choice_d: Complete the form required under s. 452.05(1)(i)
explanation: Section 452.12(5)(d) states: 'At the time of renewal, each broker or salesperson who is an individual shall complete the form under s. 452.05 (1) (i).'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Wis. Stat. 452.12(3)'s limitation on a firm's responsibility for the brokerage services of an associated licensee is expressly made 'subject to' which other statutory provision?
choice_a: Section 452.139(3), concerning a firm's liability for negligent hiring
choice_b: Section 452.14(4m), concerning required education or training imposed as discipline
choice_c: Section 452.17(1), concerning criminal penalties for unlicensed practice
choice_d: Section 452.132(6), concerning a licensee's duty to discuss document errors with a party
explanation: Section 452.12(3) begins: 'Subject to s. 452.139 (3), a firm is responsible for the brokerage services provided on behalf of the firm by a licensee associated with the firm only to the extent that the firm fails to comply with s. 452.132...' -- s. 452.139(3) addresses liability for negligent hiring.

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.01(4x), what is a 'licensed broker business entity'?
choice_a: A sole proprietorship operated by a licensed individual broker
choice_b: A broker licensed under s. 452.12 that is a business entity
choice_c: Any business entity that employs at least one licensed salesperson
choice_d: A business entity registered with DSPS but not yet issued a broker's license
explanation: Section 452.01(4x) defines: '"Licensed broker business entity" means a broker licensed under s. 452.12 that is a business entity.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.01(4y), what is a 'licensed individual broker'?
choice_a: An individual broker who works exclusively as a business representative for a business entity
choice_b: An individual salesperson who has accumulated at least 40 experience points
choice_c: A broker licensed under s. 452.12 who is an individual
choice_d: Any individual who has passed the broker's examination but has not yet been issued a license
explanation: Section 452.01(4y) defines: '"Licensed individual broker" means a broker licensed under s. 452.12 who is an individual.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Wis. Admin. Code REEB 23.01 states that the rules in ch. REEB 23 are adopted pursuant to which statutes?
choice_a: Sections 452.14, 452.17, and 452.19, Stats., the discipline and penalty provisions
choice_b: Sections 440.01 and 440.03, Stats., only
choice_c: Section 452.132, Stats., alone
explanation: REEB 23.01 provides: 'The rules in this chapter are adopted pursuant to ss. 227.11, 452.07, 452.09, 452.10 and 452.12, Stats.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 23.03(1), how is a 'trade name' defined?
choice_a: The name, other than the name appearing on the license, under which a licensed individual broker or a licensed broker business entity advertises or does business
choice_b: Any name a licensee uses on a personal social media account
choice_c: The legal name of the firm's parent corporation, if the firm is a subsidiary
choice_d: A name reserved with the Secretary of State but not yet approved by the board
explanation: REEB 23.03(1) defines: '"Trade name" means the name other than the name appearing on the license, under which the licensed individual broker or a licensed broker business entity advertises or does business.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 23.03(2), when must a licensee notify the department of a trade name?
choice_a: Annually at renewal, regardless of when the trade name was first used
choice_b: Before doing business under any trade name, the licensee shall notify the department in writing of the trade name
choice_c: Within 30 days after first using the trade name in advertising
choice_d: Only if the trade name differs from the licensee's legal name by more than one word
explanation: REEB 23.03(2) states: 'A licensee, before doing business under any trade name, shall notify the department in writing of the trade name.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 23.04(1), what must a licensed broker business entity that intends to conduct business under a different business type do?
choice_a: Notify the department within 60 days after the change, with no new application required
choice_b: Obtain board approval only if the business-type change involves a merger with another entity
choice_c: Apply for a new license, and upon payment of the fee specified in s. 440.05(1), be issued a license under the new business type
choice_d: Simply file a no-cost amendment to its existing license reflecting the new business type
explanation: REEB 23.04(1) provides: 'A licensed broker business entity who intends to conduct business under a different business type, shall apply for a new license. Upon payment of the fee specified in s. 440.05 (1), Stats., the board shall issue to the applicant a license under the new business type.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(1), what two conditions must be satisfied before a licensee may provide brokerage services on behalf of a firm?
choice_a: The licensee must be associated with the firm and must have completed continuing education that calendar year
choice_b: The firm must be debt-free, and the licensee must carry errors-and-omissions insurance
choice_c: The licensee need only be associated with the firm; notifying the department is optional
choice_d: The licensee must be associated with the firm, and the licensee must have notified the department that the licensee is associated with the firm
explanation: Section 452.30(1) states: 'No licensee may provide brokerage services on behalf of a firm unless all of the following apply: (a) The licensee is associated with the firm. (b) The licensee has notified the department that the licensee is associated with the firm.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(2)(a), how may a licensee notify the department of firm association without paying a separate notification fee?
choice_a: By providing the notice at the time the licensee first applies for licensure as a broker or salesperson
choice_b: By mailing a signed letter to the board chairperson at any time after licensure
choice_c: By including the notice on the licensee's continuing education completion certificate
choice_d: There is no fee-free method; a transfer fee always applies to any firm-association notice
explanation: Section 452.30(2)(a) provides that a licensee may notify the department of firm association 'by providing the notice at the time the licensee first applies for licensure as a broker or salesperson,' and 'no separate fee for notifying the department may be required for such a notification under this paragraph.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(2)(b), aside from notifying at the time of initial license application, how else may a licensee notify the department of association with a firm?
choice_a: By waiting for the department to update its records automatically at the licensee's next renewal
choice_b: By notifying the department through a form prescribed by the department and paying the transfer fee specified in s. 440.05(7)
choice_c: By having the firm's business representative certify the association orally to the board
choice_d: By submitting a notarized affidavit, for which no fee is required under any circumstance
explanation: Section 452.30(2)(b) allows notification 'through the use of a form prescribed by the department and paying the transfer fee specified in s. 440.05 (7).'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(3), what method must a licensee who is already associated with one firm use to notify the department of becoming associated with another firm?
choice_a: The licensee's original firm alone is responsible for notifying the department of the change
choice_b: The fee-free method under sub. (2)(a), since it is not the licensee's first association with a firm
choice_c: The method specified in sub. (2)(b) -- a department-prescribed form accompanied by the transfer fee under s. 440.05(7)
choice_d: No notification is required as long as the licensee's total period of employment does not lapse
explanation: Section 452.30(3) states: 'A licensee who is associated with a firm may notify the department that the licensee has become associated with another firm using the method specified in sub. (2) (b).'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(4)(b), when a firm terminates a licensee's association with the firm, what must the firm do?
choice_a: Notify only the terminated licensee directly; no filing with the department is required
choice_b: Wait until the firm's next biennial renewal to report the termination to the department
choice_c: Report the termination only if the terminated individual was serving as the firm's supervising broker
choice_d: Through the use of a form prescribed by the department, send written notice of the termination to the department within 10 days after the termination
explanation: Section 452.30(4)(b) provides: 'A firm that terminates a licensee from being associated with the firm shall, through the use of a form prescribed by the department, send written notice of that termination to the department within 10 days after the termination.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(5), if a firm's license is suspended or revoked, what happens to a licensee who is associated with that firm?
choice_a: The licensee may not be associated with the firm during the period of suspension or revocation, but may become associated with another firm if the licensee was not a party to the activities causing the suspension or revocation
choice_b: The licensee's own individual license is automatically suspended for the same period as the firm's
choice_c: The licensee must wait until the firm's suspension or revocation is fully lifted before joining any other firm
choice_d: The licensee may continue working for the suspended firm on a probationary basis pending board review
explanation: Section 452.30(5) states: 'No licensee may be associated with a firm if the firm's license has been suspended or revoked during the period of suspension or revocation. The licensee may become associated with another firm, provided the licensee is not a party to the activities causing the suspension or revocation of the firm's license.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Continuing from Wis. Stat. 452.30(5), after a licensee whose firm was suspended or revoked becomes associated with a new firm, when may the licensee begin providing brokerage services on behalf of that new firm?
choice_a: After a mandatory 30-day waiting period regardless of whether notification has been given
choice_b: Only after the licensee has satisfied the notification requirement under sub. (1)(b) as to the new firm
choice_c: Immediately upon signing an employment or independent-contractor agreement with the new firm
choice_d: Only after the new firm's next biennial license renewal has been completed
explanation: Section 452.30(5) concludes: 'If the licensee becomes associated with another firm, the licensee may not provide brokerage services on behalf of that firm until sub. (1) (b) has been satisfied' -- i.e., until the department is notified of the new association.

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(6)(a), what must a broker who is associated with a firm obtain before also engaging in independent real estate practice under his or her own name or a licensed broker business entity's name?
choice_a: Approval solely from the Real Estate Examining Board, without any need for firm approval
choice_b: Nothing; brokers may freely engage in independent practice without any approval
choice_c: Written approval from, and avoidance of conflicts of interest with, each firm with which the broker is associated
choice_d: A separate license issued specifically for independent-practice brokers
explanation: Section 452.30(6)(a) states: 'A broker who is associated with a firm may also engage in independent real estate practice in his or her own name or under the name of a licensed broker business entity, if the broker obtains written approval from and avoids conflicts of interest with each firm with which the broker is associated.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(6)(a)1 and 2, what must the written approval for a broker's independent practice specify?
choice_a: The broker's projected annual commission income and tax filing status
choice_b: The specific properties the broker is authorized to list independently
choice_c: The board's fee schedule applicable to independent-practice licenses
choice_d: Whether the broker may engage other licensees to work under the broker, and that the broker is responsible for supervising any licensees associated with the broker in that independent practice
explanation: Section 452.30(6)(a) requires the written approval to specify '1. Whether the broker engaging in independent practice may engage other licensees to work under the broker. 2. That the broker engaging in independent practice is responsible for the supervision of any licensees associated with the broker.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(6)(b), before engaging in independent practice, what must a broker do?
choice_a: Notify the department of that fact and of the name under which the broker will engage in independent practice
choice_b: Publish a public notice of the intended independent practice in a newspaper of general circulation
choice_c: Obtain a separate broker's license issued solely for independent practice
choice_d: Wait 90 days after receiving each firm's written approval before beginning independent practice
explanation: Section 452.30(6)(b) states: 'Before engaging in independent practice as provided in par. (a), a broker shall notify the department of that fact and of the name under which the broker will engage in independent practice.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(6)(c), with respect to a broker's independent practice activities, how is the broker's relationship to a firm that approved that independent practice treated?
choice_a: The independent practice is legally treated as a branch office of the approving firm
choice_b: The broker is not considered to be associated with that firm with respect to the broker's independent practice activities
choice_c: The broker remains fully associated with and supervised by that firm for all independent-practice transactions
choice_d: The approving firm becomes jointly and severally liable for the broker's independent-practice transactions
explanation: Section 452.30(6)(c) provides: 'A broker that is engaging in independent practice shall not be considered to be associated with a firm that approved the broker engaging in independent practice under par. (a) with respect to the broker's independent practice activities.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.30(7)(a), how many firms may a salesperson be associated with at a given time?
choice_a: Any number of firms, as long as the salesperson notifies the department of each
choice_b: No limit is imposed by statute on how many firms a salesperson may be associated with
choice_c: Only one firm at a given time
choice_d: Up to two firms, provided both consent in writing
explanation: Section 452.30(7)(a) states plainly: 'A salesperson may be associated with only one firm at a given time.'

topic: License Issuance, Renewal, Status Changes & Firm Registration
question: A licensed broker moves from Firm A, where the broker is treated as an employee, to become an independent contractor of Firm B. Which of the following actions, drawn from Wis. Stat. 452.30, correctly matches what the broker or Firm A must do?
choice_a: Only Firm A has any notification obligation, and it must notify the department within 30 days of the broker's departure
choice_b: No notification to the department is required as long as the broker's real estate license itself remains current
choice_c: The broker must reapply for an entirely new individual broker's license before joining Firm B
choice_d: The broker must notify the department of the new association with Firm B using the method under sub. (2)(b), and may not act on Firm B's behalf until that notification requirement is satisfied
explanation: Under s. 452.30(3), a licensee already associated with a firm notifies the department of a new firm association using the method in sub. (2)(b) (a department-prescribed form and the transfer fee under s. 440.05(7)), and under sub. (1) the licensee may not provide brokerage services on behalf of the new firm until that notification requirement is satisfied.
